officials.name: Colin Nash
officials.hours: Monday - Friday, 8:00 a.m. - 5:00 p.m. Closed Holidays
officials.bio: Colin Nash is an attorney who has been twice elected to represent Boise’s West Bench in the Idaho Legislature. As a state lawmaker, Nash strengthened Idaho’s sexual assault laws, defended the City of Boise’s renter protection ordinance, helped advance meaningful housing affordability measures, and developed a track record of fiscal responsibility. Colin and his wife Hailey are renters in Boise’s Winstead Park neighborhood where they live with their two young children.

officials.name: Jimmy Hallyburton
officials.hours: Monday - Friday, 8:00 a.m. - 5:00 p.m. Closed Holidays
officials.bio: Jimmy Hallyburton was born and raised on the rural edges of NW Boise. After fighting wildfires and graduating from Boise State University, he created a nonprofit called the Boise Bicycle Project (BBP) in 2007. He was elected to Boise City Council in 2019 and reelected in 2023 as the representative for District 6.

officials.name: Jordan Morales
officials.hours: Monday - Friday, 8:00 a.m. - 5:00 p.m. Closed Holidays
officials.bio: Jordan Morales was elected to the Boise City Council in 2023 as the first representative to serve from District 4, which encompasses Southeast Boise and the Vista Bench. His priorities on the council include housing affordability, safe streets, transportation, and climate action. Professionally, Jordan manages business operations for Boise State University's Department of Computer Science.

officials.name: Luci Willits
officials.hours: Monday - Friday, 8:00 a.m. - 5:00 p.m. Closed Holidays
officials.bio: Luci Willits, a lifelong Idahoan, brings a unique blend of experience and dedication to her role as Boise City Council member for District 1. With a background in both private and public sectors and 20 years as a West Boise resident, she has a deep understanding of the issues facing the city. First elected in 2021 and re-elected in 2023, Luci's priorities include public safety, library access, and maintaining and expanding Boise’s beautiful parks.

officials.name: Meredith Stead
officials.hours: Monday - Friday, 8:00 a.m. - 5:00 p.m. Closed Holidays
officials.bio: Meredith Stead lived in a few different places before calling Boise home, graduating from the University of Colorado with a BA in Communication and English Literature. Her career included work in independent film and launching the San Francisco Ski and Snowboard Festival. Appointed by Mayor McLean in 2023, she was elected to a four-year term and selected by her peers to serve as Council President.

officials.name: Kathy Corless
officials.hours: Monday - Friday, 8:00 a.m. - 5:00 p.m. Closed Holidays
officials.bio: Kathy Corless is a third-generation Boise resident, hailing from the scenic Boise Bench area. With a rich background deeply rooted in the local community, Kathy brings a wealth of experience and dedication to her role. Kathy was elected to the Boise City Council representing District 3 in November of 2023 and is serving a four-year term.

officials.name: Chris Allgood
officials.bio: Councilmember Chris Allgood's family moved to Idaho in 1976. He served the citizens of Caldwell for 30 years with the Caldwell Police Department, including 8 years as Chief of Police before retiring in 2015. Chris became a proud member of the City Council in 2016 and was re-elected in 2017 and 2019, with his current term ending December 31, 2027.

officials.name: Chuck Stadick
officials.bio: Councilmember Chuck Stadick was born in Minnesota, served in the U.S. Army, and had a long career with J.R. Simplot Company before retiring. He has been actively involved in the Caldwell community, serving on various boards and commissions, and previously held a seat on the City Council from 2016 to 2019. Chuck enjoys fishing, golf, and spending time with his family.

officials.name: Diana Register
officials.bio: Councilmember Diana Register has lived in Idaho since 2006 and has a long history in law enforcement, including civilian employee positions at Caldwell and Nampa police departments. She is an international best-selling author, local realtor, small business owner, and Chairman of the IAM149 public charity. Diana was elected to the Caldwell City Council in 2021, with her current term ending December 31, 2029.

officials.name: Geoff Williams
officials.bio: Councilmember Geoff Williams and his wife Beth made Caldwell their home in 2007, where they raised their family and served the community. His diverse career includes managing small businesses, banking, missionary work, and serving as a pastor and Caldwell Police Chaplain. Appointed on February 16, 2022, his priorities are faith, family, and community.

officials.name: Mike Dittenber
officials.bio: Mike Dittenber is a 50+ year Canyon County resident who made Caldwell his community of choice 25 years ago. He has been the Executive Director of the Caldwell Housing Authority since January 2, 2007, and previously worked for Idaho Housing and Finance Association and the Boise Police Department. He is a Veteran of the United States Marine Corp and was educated at Boise State University.

officials.name: Scott Tilmant
officials.bio: Councilmember Scott Tilmant was born in Salt Lake City, Utah, and lived overseas before returning to the US to start a civil drafting and service business. He moved to Caldwell in 1998, where he has served the community through Scouting and on the Impact Fee Advisory Board. Elected in 2025, he began his term on the Caldwell City Council in January 2026.

Constitutional and statutory laws give this one elective county office (Clerk) five distinct titles: Clerk of the District Court, Auditor, Recorder, Clerk of the Board of County Commissioners, Chief Elections Officer of the County.

officials.name: Brad Holton
officials.hours: Weekdays 8am - 5pm *Closed for lunch 12pm-1pm (excluding holidays)
officials.bio: Brad Holton is a lifelong resident of Canyon County, where he has run a local small business for over 46 years and served as Mayor of Greenleaf for 27 years. He is honored to serve as Commissioner for District 2 and Chairman of the Board of County Commissioners, committed to leading with transparency and accountability.

officials.name: Leslie Van Beek
officials.hours: Weekdays 8am - 5pm *Closed for lunch 12pm-1pm (excluding holidays)
officials.bio: Leslie Van Beek is an Idaho native, born and raised in the Treasure Valley. She has a degree in Health Science and a minor in Biology, with work experience in banking, retail, and public relations. She now serves as the District 1 Commissioner for Canyon County, committed to honest and fair representation of its citizens.

officials.name: Zach Brooks

officials.name: Chris Boyd
officials.hours: Weekdays 8am - 5pm (excluding holidays)
officials.bio: As your Prosecuting Attorney, Chris Boyd's duty is to uphold the law, protect the community, and ensure that justice is served. His office is committed to holding criminals accountable while supporting victims and maintaining the integrity of the legal system. He has built a team of highly skilled professionals dedicated to making Canyon County safer and ensuring effective government functions.

officials.name: Brandon Lee
officials.address: City of Idaho Falls 308 Constitution Way Idaho Falls, ID 83402
officials.bio: Brandon was elected to serve on the Idaho Falls City Council in December of 2025. He was born and raised in Idaho Falls and has been involved in real estate acquisition and development for the past 19 years. He earned his CPA and holds an MBA, and has a passion for coaching youth soccer.

officials.name: Jim Freeman
officials.address: City of Idaho Falls 308 Constitution Way Idaho Falls, ID 83402
officials.bio: Jim Freeman, a lifelong Idaho Falls resident, followed his family's tradition of civic service, eventually serving 26 years with the Idaho Falls Fire Department as a firefighter, paramedic, and Captain. Since retiring in 2012, he has actively volunteered and served on various boards, including the Mayor's Citizen Review Committee for Parks and Recreation and the Golf Advisory Board. He is proud to serve the citizens of Idaho Falls as a Council Member.

officials.name: John Radford
officials.address: City of Idaho Falls 308 Constitution Way Idaho Falls, ID 83402

officials.name: Kirk Larsen
officials.address: City of Idaho Falls 308 Constitution Way Idaho Falls, ID 83402
officials.bio: Kirk was elected to serve on the Idaho Falls City Council in November of 2023 and entered his first term in January 2024. Kirk is a lifelong Idahoan who grew up interested in making money work to reach goals, which led him to a successful career in banking. Kirk graduated from Brigham Young University with a bachelor's in finance, holds an MBA from Idaho State University, and earned a certificate at Pacific Coast Banking School.

officials.name: Michelle Ziel-Dingman
officials.address: City of Idaho Falls 308 Constitution Way Idaho Falls, ID 83402

officials.name: Jim Francis
officials.address: City of Idaho Falls 308 Constitution Way Idaho Falls, ID 83402
officials.bio: Jim came to Idaho Falls in 1953 at the age of four when his father took a job working with the early test reactors. Jim attended Emerson and Linden Park elementary schools and graduated from Idaho Falls High School in 1966, the last year in which there was only one high school in District 91. After leaving Idaho Falls for a few years to complete his college education and begin his teaching career, he returned to the city with his wife in 1977 as a teacher of history in the Idaho Falls school system.

officials.name: Lisa Burtenshaw
officials.address: City of Idaho Falls 308 Constitution Way Idaho Falls, ID 83402
officials.bio: Lisa Meikle Burtenshaw, raised in Idaho Falls, holds a Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering. She served on the Idaho Falls District 91 board for 10 years and the City Council before being elected Mayor in December 2025, starting her term in January 2026. She is passionate about proactive planning for the city's rapid growth.

officials.name: Roger Clark
officials.bio: Commissioner Clark is a rancher and lifelong resident of Jefferson County. He was elected to a four-year term in 2018, re-elected to a two-year term in 2022 and re-elected to a four-year term in 2024. He and his wife live in Menan.

officials.name: Scott Hancock
officials.bio: Commissioner Hancock is a rancher and retired from the INL. He was elected to a two-year term in 2014, re-elected to a four-year term in 2016, re-elected to a two-year term in 2020 and re-elected to a four-year term in 2022. He and his wife live in Rigby.

officials.name: Shayne Young
officials.bio: Commissioner Young is a business owner and lifelong resident of Jefferson County. He was elected to a two-year term in 2018, re-elected to a four year term in 2020 and re-elected to a two-year term in 2024. He and his wife live in Labelle.

officials.name: Dale Reynolds
officials.bio: Dale Reynolds was elected to District 4 in November 2023 and sworn into office for a four-year term on January 2, 2024. An Idaho native, he has lived in Nampa for eight years and owns Icon Mechanical. He has served in various community roles, including the Treasure Valley God and Country Festival board and as a Wyakin Warrior Foundation mentor.

officials.name: David Bills
officials.bio: David Bills was appointed to the Nampa City Council in January 2024 and later voted Council President in 2026. A graduate of Borah High School and Boise State University, he and his wife Carrie have been active in real estate, construction, and development in Nampa since 1994 through their company Lanco, Inc. Bills has also led various Biblical ministries and previously served on the Nampa City Council and Meridian School District School Board.

officials.name: Debbie Skaug
officials.bio: Debbie Skaug was elected to the Nampa City Council in November of 2025 and sworn in January 5, 2026. Debbie is a native Idahoan, raised on a wheat farm in south central Idaho. She has supported or served with numerous Nampa charitable organizations as a volunteer.

officials.name: Natalie Jangula
officials.hours: M-F 8am-5pm
officials.bio: Natalie Jangula was sworn into office for District 2 on January 2, 2024. She is a Financial Advisor Administrative Assistant and is actively involved in community service, including the Nampa Lions Club and volunteering at her children's schools. Councilwoman Jangula is committed to upholding Nampa's vision of a caring community with economic opportunity and a unique identity.

officials.name: Sebastian Griffin
officials.bio: Sebastian Griffin was sworn in as a Nampa City Councilman for District 6 on January 2, 2024. A 5th generation Idahoan and Nampa native, he is a small business owner and is currently pursuing a joint Juris Doctor and Masters in Accounting and Taxation at the University of Idaho, College of Law.

officials.name: Victor Rodriguez
officials.bio: Victor Rodriguez was elected to the Nampa City Council in November of 2017 and re-elected in November of 2021 and November of 2025 to District 5. He retired from the Nampa Police Department in 2012 after serving 40 years as a police officer, including 30 years as a homicide detective. Victor is married to Delsie Rodriguez, and they have 7 children and 20 grandchildren.
